The adapter keeps the module's existing _deadline_tool/_run_under_deadline idiom, splitting body-start from body-await rather than forking a second deadline path.
justifications.goal_fidelity: A retried read with the same tool and arguments joins the body still running: _deadline_tool routes kind=='read' through _read_joining_running (reckon/mcp.py:636), which keys a running body's future by (label, json(kwargs)) in _INFLIGHT_READS (reckon/mcp.py:432,565,584-588) and awaits it under asyncio.shield (reckon/mcp.py:493). Independently reproduced: a spinning read issued twice, the second after the first's 0.2 s deadline, executes one body that answers both calls (first storage-slow, retry ok), and a read with different arguments keys its own body while a write (kind!='read') still runs _run_under_deadline and is never registered.
justifications.reuse: The change reuses _deadline_seconds, the thread CPU/run-queue diagnostics, bound_response and the module's single-default-executor model; _run_under_deadline is refactored into _start_body + _await_body with no behavioural fork for writes. No capability is duplicated and no new dependency is introduced.
